What is ready, and what needs integration?

Start with the application's existing capabilities and identify the configuration or business implementation you need.

Included in the template

Accounts and sessions

Password sign-in, registration and password-recovery pages, session handling, and sign-out. API keys identify programmatic requests.

Configuration required

Registration and email

Define registration and password rules. Email verification and password recovery require a working mail channel and integration with the authentication flow.

Integration required

Company and third-party sign-in

Connect an identity provider and define account linking. These sign-in options are not enabled by default.

What to know before you use it

Verify these boundaries alongside the business feature.

Identity and access are different

Authentication identifies the user. Authorization determines which pages, records, and actions that user can access.

Check the whole session lifecycle

Verify sign-out, expiration, account disabling, and re-enabling. Protect server APIs as well as pages.

scenarios.summary: Open a task, use the actions the business allows, and refresh after handling.
decisions: Example
Approving an expense moves it to completed and reduces the pending count.
checks: Only people allowed to handle the work can view details and act.
Handling refreshes lists and all related counts.
scenarios.note: Try test records first, then adapt to your business.

scenarios.title: Try the flow with two accounts
scenarios.summary: Ask the Agent to verify real business work, then try it yourself.
decisions: Example
Alex handles Alex’s work; Jordan cannot read or handle Alex’s personal entries.
checks: Isolation between two accounts is verified.
Executed and unexecuted scenarios are reported separately.
scenarios.note: Try test records first, then adapt to your business.

scenarios.title: Connect ordinary work
scenarios.summary: Collection, missing documents and delivery confirmation can be tasks without approval stages.
decisions: Example
Issuing EQ-001 to Alex creates work; confirming receipt completes it.
checks: The same work does not appear twice.
Successful collection completes the item; failed collection leaves it pending.
scenarios.note: Try test records first, then adapt to your business.

scenarios.title: See how much work remains
scenarios.summary: Show the pending count without opening the full list.
decisions: Example
Two expense tasks and one equipment task give an all-source badge of 3.
checks: The dashboard count matches the task list it opens.
Business filters show matching work; switching accounts shows only that account’s work.
scenarios.note: Try test records first, then adapt to your business.

scenarios.title: Transfer work to someone else
scenarios.summary: Cancel the former recipient’s unfinished entry and create work for the new recipient.
decisions: Example
Equipment work moves from Alex to Jordan; only Jordan can confirm receipt.
checks: Former recipients cannot handle reassigned work.
Completed history is retained; unfinished work is cancelled as specified.
scenarios.note: Try test records first, then adapt to your business.

scenarios.title: Bring existing work into the center
scenarios.summary: Show old and new work together in an application already in use.
decisions: Example
A paused backfill resumes without restoring pending status over online completion.
checks: Interrupted batches resume without duplicate entries.
Completed work never becomes pending again.
scenarios.note: Try test records first, then adapt to your business.

scenarios.title: Notify recipients when work arrives
scenarios.summary: A notification signals work to do; completion still happens in the business.
decisions: Example
Reading a collection reminder does not complete the task.
checks: One reminder per business event and recipient.
Reading does not complete tasks; delivery failure does not undo business writes.
